newsitem.title: USA: GM paid $67 mln to settle door-latch claims.
newsitem.headline: GM paid $67 mln to settle door-latch claims.

text.p: General Motors Corp. paid more than $67 million to settle 55 lawsuits alleging that door latches, like those installed in some 40 million GM cars and trucks, were defective and caused deaths and injuries, an Alabama judge disclosed Thursday.

Ruling in post-trial motions in a case that resulted in a $150 million jury verdict against GM in June, District Judge Ted Bozeman in Lowndes County, Ala., decided the settlement information was not confidential and should be disclosed.

Lawyers for Alex and Thelma Hardy sought the disclosure in order to contest GM's post-trial claims that the $150 million jury verdict in June -- the largest ever against an automaker -- was excessive.

The Hardys had sued GM alleging that Alex was paralyzed in a 1991 roll-over wreck when the door latch on his 1987 Chevrolet S-10 Blazer sport/utility vehicle failed, causing him to be thrown from the truck.
Jim Butler, a lawyer for the Hardys, said in a statement that the settlements, averaging $1.2 million from 1984 through 1996, show that GM was trying to cover up problems with the latches.
"It's incredible that GM would continue to protest this door latch is not defective in the face of all these settlements," Butler said.
GM has steadfastly maintained that the $3 "Type III" latches, which were installed in over 40 million North American cars and trucks from 1978 to 1987, are safe.
It said it recently submitted data to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on laboratory tests, crash tests and actual accidents showing the latch to be an "outstanding design."
"Just because we settled some cases, doesn't mean there's a defective door latch -- or a defect period," GM spokesman Kyle Johnson said Friday.
GM is appealing the Hardy verdict.
